title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: Unlike iron and cobalt clusters, which deflect only toward the strong field and fit superparamagnetism, gadolinium, terbium, and dysprosium clusters show two size-dependent Stern-Gerlach responses: a sharp superparamagnetic profile or a broad locked-moment profile.
explanation: The authors contrast transition-metal superparamagnetism with rare-earth size dependence already known for gadolinium and reproduced for terbium and, preliminarily, dysprosium. Superparamagnetism gives a sharp peak; locked-moment clusters give a broad peak spanning strong- and weak-field deflections.
scope: Neutral Gd, Tb, and Dy clusters in gradient-magnet deflection experiments; Fe and Co clusters only as the contrasting superparamagnetic case.
conditions: Laser-vaporization beam, collimation, Stern-Gerlach deflection, then excimer ionization and time-of-flight detection. Superparamagnetic at all studied temperatures: Gd22, Tb17, Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, and Dy27.
caveats: Dysprosium results are described as preliminary. Which model applies is size specific, not a single rare-earth rule.
